subject: ss-plastic-surgery
title: Autologous Breast Reconstruction: DIEP, TRAM Zones and Donor Sites

steps.say: Borrowed abdominal tissue is rebuilding the breast mound without weakening the belly wall. The deep inferior epigastric perforator flap is carrying skin with fat while completely sparing the rectus muscle and its sheath. Abdominal strength is surviving the harvest because no muscle travels with the flap.
steps.tx: The **DIEP flap** transfers abdominal skin and fat while completely sparing the **rectus abdominis** muscle and **anterior rectus sheath**. No muscle travels, so the abdominal wall stays strong. The **perforator** vessels alone supply the whole transplanted tissue island. Muscle-sparing harvest is keeping hernia and bulge rates near zero.

steps.say: Transplanted tissue is needing chest vessels of matching size for the anastomosis. The chest recipient is usually the internal mammary pair sitting in the third or fourth rib interspace. Removing one cartilage segment is exposing the vessels for a comfortable size match.
steps.tx: The **internal mammary artery (IMA)** with its vein in the **third or fourth** rib space is the primary **recipient vessel** of the chest, and both **recipient vessels** are prepared together. Cartilage removal exposes the pair for a size match with the deep inferior epigastric pedicle. Reliable inflow is deciding flap survival from the first stitch.

steps.say: Older pedicled flaps are teaching zone selection for the modern free flap. Zone one over the pedicle is perfusing best, zone four at the far contralateral corner is failing worst. The least perfused corner is routinely discarded before inset begins.
steps.tx: **Hartrampf zones** (**TRAM zones**) map TRAM perfusion: **Zone I** over the pedicle enjoys the richest flow, **Zone II** covers the opposite medial half, **Zone III** the same-side lateral half, while far-corner **Zone IV** is least perfused and discarded. Zone selection is preventing fat necrosis at the far corner.

steps.say: Some abdomens are offering a superficial system strong enough to skip the fascia entirely. The superficial inferior epigastric artery flap is avoiding the rectus sheath in about twenty to thirty percent of patients. A caliber over one point five millimetres is marking the systems that can carry a whole breast.
steps.tx: The **SIEA flap** avoids the **rectus sheath** entirely but suits only **20% to 30%** of patients with caliber over **1.5 mm**. The **superficial** system must prove adequate on imaging. Smaller vessels cannot perfuse a whole breast and force conversion to DIEP.

steps.say: Used-up abdomens are turning the plan toward the back for reliable tissue. The latissimus dorsi flap pedicled on the thoracodorsal vessels is swinging skin with muscle forward. An implant beneath the muscle is supplying final volume in thinner patients.
steps.tx: The **latissimus dorsi** myocutaneous flap on the **thoracodorsal vessels** gives reliable autologous tissue, often with an **implant** beneath for volume. The pedicled swing avoids microsurgery entirely and never fails from anastomotic thrombosis. Thinner patients need the implant boost to reach symmetry with the opposite breast.

steps.say: Thighs and buttocks are donating when the abdomen cannot serve at all. The transverse upper gracilis, profunda artery perforator, and superior gluteal artery perforator flaps are covering the secondary choices. Each donor is matching specific body shapes and prior surgical histories.
steps.tx: Secondary free flaps cover unsuitable abdomens: **TUG flap** from the inner thigh, **PAP flap** from the posterior thigh, and **SGAP flap** from the buttock. Each **donor site** matches body habitus and scar history. Choice is balancing volume needs against donor morbidity.

steps.say: Radiated chests are hardening around implants and failing at several times the normal rate. Post-mastectomy radiation is multiplying contracture and failure rates by three to four times. Autologous tissue with its own blood supply is softening instead and becoming the preferred modality.
steps.tx: **Post-mastectomy radiation (PMRT)** raises contracture and **implant failure** rates **3 to 4 times**, so **autologous reconstruction** is preferred. Implants harden under radiation while living tissue softens and stays supple for years. Irradiated chests strongly favour living flaps over prosthetic implants every time.

rows: Failure up three to four times

steps.say: Blind exploration for the best vessel is wasting hours in the operating theatre. Preoperative CT angiography is mapping the single largest dominant perforator before incision. Tracing its intramuscular trajectory is letting the surgeon commit to the best vessel immediately.
steps.tx: Preoperative abdominal **CT angiography** maps the single largest dominant **perforator** and its **intramuscular trajectory**, cutting **DIEP** operative time. The surgeon commits to the best vessel before the first incision is ever made. Imaging turns blind exploration into planned and predictable dissection for the team.
